data.title: With ‘Digger,’ Tom Cruise Takes On His Riskiest Business Yet
data.incipit: “I was very successful since I was a kid,” Cruise told a packed Academy Museum screening. With his latest film, the actor, and Oscar-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu, are putting that star power to the test.
data.body: “I was very successful since I was a kid,” Tom Cruise told a full house at the Academy Museum ’s 945-seat David Geffen Theater following a screening of Digger . That stardom has led him in search of ever bigger challenges, learning new skills and finding opportunities to apply them. As he put it: “OK, the door’s open. Now I want to push it again.” He has certainly done that with Digger , Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s wildly ambitious, deeply weird and extravagantly mounted comedy, in which Cruise plays a Texas oil tycoon forced to face the music after an environmental disaster puts the world at risk. The Warner Bros. release, arriving just as Paramount nears its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, carries a reported $125 million production budget. At 64 and 63, respectively, Cruise and Iñárritu are near-exact contemporaries taking this leap together. Cruise has ventured into similarly offbeat territory before, memorably in an Oscar-nominated turn in Paul Thomas Anderson’s Magnolia and beneath the prosthetics of Ben Stiller’s comedy Tropic Thunder . But he has spent much of his recent career delivering increasingly elaborate Mission: Impossible spectacles, taking extraordinary physical risks within a franchise whose appeal he understands intimately. Digger requires a different leap of faith, both from Cruise and from the audience he hopes will follow him. Among critics, the film has proved wildly divisive , with some reviews positively savage, The Hollywood Reporter ’s among them . I understand the objections to Digger ; I was also quite happy to have seen it. There is something invigorating about watching this much talent and money committed to a movie this peculiar, even when its considerable parts refuse to cooperate. Tom Cruise talks to the audience at Academy Museum’s ‘Digger’ screening. Seth Abramovitch Iñárritu offered a remarkably candid account of the challenges during the discussion. Making this trompe-l’œil of a film required a constant negotiation between theatricality and the camera. What felt inspired on set could look very different the following morning. “We were laughing all day,” the four-time Oscar-winning Mexican filmmaker said. Then he would watch the dailies: “Oh my God,” he recalled thinking. “This is not working. This is shit.” Adjusting the performance could send it too far in the other direction: “It’s too naturalistic. It’s not so funny.” In sharing that, Iñárritu was describing the search for the film’s highly unusual tone, not conceding that the finished movie had failed. But the anecdote gets at the precariousness of the enterprise. The actors had to find that tone in their bodies and voices, he explained. “Nothing can be written in tone. It doesn’t exist,” he said. Iñárritu compared the precision of Cruise’s acting to the “micro decisions” he makes during a dangerous stunt, when “one second is the difference between life and death.” On set, the director watched that attention extend to where Cruise placed his hands, when he winked and when he stayed silent. “Every take he’s just present and observing naturally,” he said. Cruise, meanwhile, seemed delighted by the company he was keeping. He repeatedly jumped in to praise his fellow actors, recalling how difficult it was to stop laughing around John Goodman. Of Sandra Hüller, he said, “What an extraordinary actress,” before settling on a succession of wows. His enthusiasm was considerably easier to pin down than his acting techniques. After Cruise gave a drawn-out answer about a life spent observing humanity to explain his character work, Iñárritu teased him: “He keeps the secret. He don’t answer.” Tom Cruise and Alejandro G. Iñárritu at the Academy Museum’s ‘Digger’ screening. Seth Abramovitch By the end of the conversation, Cruise was making a broader argument about what audiences want, and what filmmakers should give them. “This film is handmade,” he said. He described stopping on set with his colleagues to look around and appreciate the skill that had gone into the physical world surrounding them. “People want to see real things,” he said. Then, a little later: “People want real things and they want real experiences.” Cruise never mentioned artificial intelligence, but the repeated emphasis on “real things” and “handmade” filmmaking could readily be heard as an implicit rejoinder to it. His remarks placed the value in the people doing the work, the skills they had acquired and the pleasure of being together to make something. “It was never handed to any of us,” he said. For all his confidence, there was also an acknowledgment that the opportunity to keep doing this depends on people buying tickets. “My hope is always that the films would do enough that I’d have that opportunity to do it again,” Cruise said. Whether audiences follow him into Digger remains to be seen. For now, he seemed grateful to have made the leap. “It’s not like I don’t have challenges, we don’t have challenges,” he said. “But I really choose to be joyful about creating.” After posing for a cast and crew photo, Cruise, ever the audience pleaser, spent 15 minutes mingling with fans who rushed the stage for selfies and a few words with a movie legend. Four decades into his career, he’s still finding new ways to make it in this risky business. He clearly loves the job.

data.title: ‘South Park’ Season 29 Episode 2 Start Time, Preview And How To Watch
data.incipit: Season 29 of Trey Parker and Matt Stone's South Park, aka South America, returns this week with its second episode after pulling in big numbers in its season premiere.In an apparent response to fans'...
data.body: Season 29 of Trey Parker and Matt Stone's South Park , aka South America , returns this week with its second episode after pulling in big numbers in its season premiere. In an apparent response to fans' dissatisfaction with Season 27 and 28's focus on President Donald Trump and his administration, Parker and Stone returned the action of the show to South Park Elementary and Cartman, Kyle, Stan and Kenny in the Season 29 premiere. 'South Park' Season 29 Release Schedule Brings Consistency After Messy 2025 The episode, called "South American Biker Gangs," lampoons the e-bike craze by having South Park's youths run rampant in the streets with their motorized bikes. Things get really ugly, though, when Randy Marsh and his gang of traditional bicyclists take resort to extreme measures to get the city to implement an e-bike ban. While Season 29's premiere episode steered clear of the White House and Trump, the air of mockery was still very much in the ether. After all, Parker and Stone didn't rename the series South America to skewer Trump's efforts to change the names of the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario to the Gulf of America and Lake America for nothing. 'Lioness' Star Laysla De Oliveira On What Season 3 Finale Means For Cruz In A Potential Season 4 In addition, the duo gets one more jab in during the show's opening sequence, which quickly features the South Park version of the president standing naked on a sidewalk and using an American flag like a bath towel. The second episode of South Park / South America Season 29 will premiere at 10 p.m. ET/PT on cable's Comedy Central and begin streaming on Paramount+ Thursday on Paramount+ at 6 a.m. ET/3 a.m. PT on Paramount+. This Week's Episode Of 'South Park' Takes On Data Centers Judging by the series' X post on Monday about this week's episode, Wednesday's setting will remain in South Park, yet will tackle an issue that cities big and small are dealing with nationwide. Per the episode's logline, Butters is unhappy that billionaires are trying to build data centers in the backyards of South Park . South Park Season 29's premiere episode attracted huge viewership in its return two weeks ago. According to Comedy Central, the show had 4.2 million multiplatform viewers across the cable channel and Paramount+ in its first three days in the U.S. 'Avengers: Endgame' Writer On Why Hawkeye Soul Stone Sacrifice Idea Was Met With Resistance "The season premiere on Comedy Central outperformed last season's premiere by double digits on persons 18-49 rating and share and was the #1 non-sports cable telecast for the week with persons 18-49," Paramount announced in a news release. New episodes of South Park / South America Season 29 will air every other week this season, with Episode 3 scheduled for Oct. 14 on Comedy Central and Oct. 15 on Paramount+. data.title: 'We're so proud of him' says sister of Emmy history-maker Matthew Rhys
data.incipit: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins27 minutes agoAngharad ThomasBBC WalesRachel EvansMatthew Rhys's sister Rachel was there with him at the Emmy Awards for his historic double...
data.body: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins 27 minutes ago Angharad Thomas BBC Wales Rachel Evans Matthew Rhys's sister Rachel was there with him at the Emmy Awards for his historic double win The sister of Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys said her family had been "pinching ourselves all week" following his historic Emmy success. Rhys became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night, after he was named best lead actor in a limited series for the psychological thriller The Beast In Me, and best lead actor in a comedy for his role in Widow's Bay. His older sister Rachel Evans, who accompanied Rhys to the ceremony in Los Angeles, said she was starstruck seeing Hollywood royalty at the event, and revealed that she and her brother called their parents afterwards, who were sat at home in their dressing gowns. "I think we just all giggled for a long time." Getty Images Rhys, who grew up in Cardiff, made history at the Emmy Awards, becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales , Evans said watching Rhys win the awards was "an experience I will never ever forget or probably match". She said that as the "bossy" older sister, she told him that morning that he needed to prepare, adding: "If you win, you cannot wing it." "We're so proud of him," she said. She also recalled the emotional moment when he thanked her during one of his acceptance speeches, calling her "the brains of the outfit". Rachel Evans / BBC Rachel and Matthew as children Evans described the moment he won as "insane". "Keri [Russell, Rhys' partner] and I just looked at each other and we just could not believe it. "Matthew's described it as surreal and it just really was." Evans said that Russell "loves to celebrate him and she's his biggest supporter", and was "just cheering, whooping, hands in the air" after his award wins. Evans said that she saw many Hollywood stars that evening, and was starstruck by Harrison Ford. "I'm a bit nervous about these things. I was just happy gaping and remembering things," she said. Despite attending multiple after-parties that evening, Evans said they made sure to video call their parents who were sat at home in their dressing gowns. "They were so far away, but they were so proud of him, as we all are... and they were pleased that I was there with him really." Evans told Owen that she unexpectedly burst into tears while watching his Emmy awards being engraved, saying that was the moment it "sank in". Evans told Owen that the response back in Wales had been "overwhelming". "We were just thrilled by the response when we woke up in the morning from home. It was just everything we could wish for," she said. In his acceptance speech, Rhys paid tribute to the "great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurturer as anyone else". "We are a small but mighty nation," he said, ending his speech with "diolch yn fawr iawn", which means "thank you very much" in Welsh. Evans said her brother has lived abroad for 25 years, but Wales "is absolutely in his heart and is his home", adding that he was "really keen to speak to everybody" the day after his wins. "Wales had been so supportive of his career all along and had really cheered him on," she added.

data.title: Fridge freezers left at Newport Docks amid suspended collections
data.incipit: Tens of thousands of fridge freezers left at docks as household collections suspended11 minutes agoOscar EdwardsBBC WalesMedia WalesThe closure of the Newport site is thought to have taken away about 30% of...
data.body: Tens of thousands of fridge freezers left at docks as household collections suspended 11 minutes ago Oscar Edwards BBC Wales Media Wales The closure of the Newport site is thought to have taken away about 30% of the fridge recycling capacity in the UK People have reported storing broken fridges and freezers in their gardens for months because some council collections have been suspended. It follows the closure of specialist treatment facilities and a wider shortage of capacity to process cooling appliances, the Local Government Authority (LGA) said. Recycling company Unimetals, which had dozens of sites in the UK, filed for liquidation in 2025 leaving tens of thousands of fridge freezers at Newport Docks. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it was working to manage the capacity shortages. Almost a quarter of Welsh councils say they have suspended household collections of fridge-freezers due to a shortage of space at disposal sites. Cardiff is one of these and Lee Young, who lives in the city, has been trying to get rid of his broken fridge-freezer for two months. "I tried to take it to the recycling centre in July but was told it wasn't accepted. Someone said the council would collect it, but they won't either." It has been sitting in his back garden ever since and he does not know when council collections will resume. Lee Young Lee Young has repurposed his old fridge freezer for plant storage overnight until he can get rid of it Lee said he was also confused by the different policies in neighbouring councils. "If I lived in Barry or Penarth (Vale of Glamorgan) they would be able to collect it from the kerb. I don't know why I can't in Cardiff." The Welsh Local Government Association has been asked why some councils are still able to carry out the collections while others are not. Michael Enea, a campaigner in Newport who blogs about fly-tipping, said he often saw the old appliances at the side of the road and thinks this could now get worse. "I think there'll be a lot of people in local communities where they don't have the ability to dispose of their fridges and freezers, who will end up literally dumping them in the street. "We see it quite a lot in Newport and right over Wales." Michael Enea Michael Enea has seen fridge freezers fly-tipped around Newport in recent months The LGA said it had identified dozens of councils across Wales and England that had been forced to stop or restrict collections, with more expected to follow suit. Associated British Ports, which took over the running of the Newport site, said it was "in discussions with third parties" about the future of the site and materials. A spokesperson added: "In the interim, the material is being managed responsibly as part of the site's transition and will be transferred to another specialist recycling operation in due course." Media Wales APB said appliances will be transferred to another specialist recycling operation in due course Dr David Santillo, a research scientist at Greenpeace, said it was possible that some of the fridges and freezers at Newport Docks still contained "some of the most harmful chemicals" such as hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs). HFCs are mainly used in air conditioning, industrial chillers and fridges, but are also powerful greenhouse gases. Chemicals such as isobutane, pentane and ammonia can also be found in commercial-type fridges, Dr Santillo added. "None of these chemicals are benign. They all have the potential for harmful effects, or they can be toxic if they leak," he said. Santillo said some older chemicals could have a "much wider impact" on the environment and leaving appliances out for long periods had the potential to produce "toxic smoke" if a fire breaks out. David Santillo Dr David Santillo has urged the UK government to improve the recycling capacity for appliances Santillo said the recycling of fridges and freezers was a national issue and he urged the UK government to "step in and find a solution". Defra said it appreciated the "challenges" facing local authorities, and was working to manage the impact of treatment capacity shortages. It added: "This includes allowing the storage of fridge and cooling equipment on temporary sites provided certain conditions set out by the Environment Agency are met." Regulator Natural Resources Wales said it was "aware of the pressures" affecting operators across the UK. It added that it was providing "regulatory flexibility" to help manage temporary storage pressures and would "continue to support efforts across the sector to restore treatment capacity and minimise disruption". The Welsh government said it was working with NRW, local authorities and the UK government to "manage the situation and support a return to normal capacity." More top stories

data.title: Queen attends charity festival amid Earl Spencer's war of words with Palace
data.incipit: Queen Camilla stepped out for a literary festival for her charity, The Queen's Reading Room, at Chatsworth House on Saturday in the midst of mounting controversy surrounding Charles Spencer's claims
data.body: Queen Camilla stepped out for a literary festival for her charity, The Queen's Reading Room, at Chatsworth House on Saturday in the midst of mounting controversy surrounding Charles Spencer's claims 19 Sep 2026, 21:56 | Updated: 7m ago Saturday marked the fourth festival at the Grade I-listed venue in the Peak District. Picture: Getty By Isobel Anderson Morris The Queen has spoken of the “life-enhancing power” of books, amid the controversy surrounding Earl Spencer’s memoir and allegations about the King’s behaviour in the wake of Diana’s death. Loading audio... Camilla received a warm reception when she was greeted at Chatsworth House in Derbyshire for the first day of her charity’s literary festival. The event was set up for the Queen’s Reading Room, a charity she founded following the success of her Instagram book club during the pandemic. Saturday marked the fourth festival at the Grade I-listed venue in the Peak District. Lord William Burlington, chairman of The Chatsworth House Trust, greeted the Queen and described it as “a huge thrill” to collaborate with The Queen’s Reading Room for a second year in a row. During a speech in the Painted Hall, Camilla said she felt as if coming back to Chatsworth House, which has a library of more than 17,000 books, was “like coming home”. Read more: Earl Spencer doubles down on claim King said ‘we’ll forget her soon enough’ in row over following Diana's coffin at funeral Read more: Queen 'offered to restore Diana's HRH' title after princess's death, Earl Spencer's memoir claims During a speech in the Painted Hall, Camilla said she felt as if coming back to Chatsworth House, which has a library of more than 17,000 books, was “like coming home”. Picture: Getty She told guests: “I created my Reading Room simply because, like all of us here, I love books and their life-enhancing power and I want to share that love with others. “In those early days, I had no idea if anybody would be interested but six years on, we are a global community of millions from over 180 countries, swapping recommendations, undertaking research and donating thousands of books to women’s refuges and homeless shelters.” She added: “There could hardly be a more fitting location for a literary festival than Chatsworth, a house that has inspired and hosted countless authors, including Charles Dickens, Elizabeth Gaskell and William Makepeace Thackeray, among many others. “Future generations will, no doubt, boast of the day when William Boyd, Elif Shafak, Robert Harris and Kate Mosse were guests here too.” Camilla’s charity event comes during the ‘war of words’ between Buckingham Palace and Earl Spencer, after he made numerous allegations over the King’s actions following Diana’s death. Camilla’s charity event comes during the ‘war of words’ between Buckingham Palace and Earl Spencer. Picture: Getty The Palace responded with an “unprecedented” response, saying “the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason”. Earl Spencer further claimed that the King sounded “giddily elated... like a lottery winner” when he rang the earl following the Princess’s death. In Spencer’s memoir, A Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, he made the accusation that Charles subjected him to a “stream of anger” after he asserted that his late sister would not have wanted her sons, Princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk in her funeral procession. During Saturday’s event, the Queen spoke with members of local book clubs at Chatsworth House, including from the Elm Foundation, a charity which provides services and support to adults and children affected by domestic abuse. Camilla later announced her four book recommendations for autumn – Finding Belle by Reeta Chakrabarti, The Picture Of Dorian Gray by Oscar Wilde, Whistler by Ann Patchett and Sashenka by Simon Sebag Montefiore. Journalist and news presenter Chakrabarti witnessed the unveiling of the chosen books and told the Queen: “Well, I don’t know what to say. Thank you so much for choosing it, and I’m going to read the others.” After the Queen's speech in the Painted Hall, she heard readings, including one by actress Natascha McElhone, best known for her parts in The Truman Show, Ronin and Solaris.

data.title: Riot Fest Ending Early Saturday As More Rain, Storms Expected In Chicago

This includes directly interviewing sources and research/analysis of primary source documents. On the Ground Indicates that a Newsmaker/Newsmakers was/were physically present to report the article from some/all of the location(s) it concerns. Sources Cited As a news piece, this article cites verifiable, third-party sources which have all been thoroughly fact-checked and deemed credible by the Newsroom. A fan records as División Minúscula performs during the first day of Riot Fest in Douglass Park in North Lawndale on Sept. 18, 2026. Credit: Colin Boyle/Block Club Chicago DOUGLASS PARK — Riot Fest is ending early Saturday as more rain and potential flooding is expected in Chicago. The festival announced the news about 3:30 p.m. after on-and-off rain all day — though Riot Fest is no stranger to rainy days and muddy grounds. “In cooperation with our partners from the City of Chicago and out of an abundance of caution for the safety of our fans, bands, and staff, Riot Fest will be ending early tonight due to inclement weather,” Riot Fest posted to social media. The new schedule is as follows: Some artists’ sets have been shortened or cut altogether. Rapper Afroman’s 8 p.m. set has been removed from the schedule. Bright Eyes was moved to the Radical Stage and pushed to 6:30 p.m. All headliners that were slated to start after 8 will now go on at 6:30 at the latest. All bands are expected to end by 7:30 p.m. The National Weather Service has issued a flood watch for the city through 7 a.m. Sunday. More rain is expected to start late Saturday afternoon with storms hitting the area around 9 p.m. Heavy rainfall is expected tonight through early Sunday morning, with a possible thunderstorm before 1 p.m. Sunday followed by a chance of showers, and the temperature falling to around 64 by 4 p.m, according to the weather service . Credit: Facebook So far Sunday’s schedule remains the same, according to Riot Fest organizers. Fest attendees can find more information and schedule updates here . data.title: Salman Khan denies health issues after Bigg Boss 20 concern
data.incipit: Bollywood actor Salman Khan has dismissed concerns about his health following an episode of Bigg Boss 20 in which he appeared unwell. During the Weekend Ka Vaar segment, Salman was seen placing his hand on...
data.body: Bollywood actor Salman Khan has dismissed concerns about his health following an episode of Bigg Boss 20 in which he appeared unwell. During the Weekend Ka Vaar segment, Salman was seen placing his hand on his heart, struggling to speak, and eventually lying down on the stage while requesting medical assistance. This sequence alarmed viewers, prompting many fans to express concern on social media. Responding to the reaction, Salman posted a statement on his Instagram Story clarifying, “Nothing is wrong with my health by the grace of God.” He criticised the editing of the show’s promotional footage, which he said created a misleading impression of a genuine health emergency. Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Salman explained that the pain he feigned was intended to make a point to contestant Qazi, who had been using his own health as entertainment. “It totally beats the purpose and looks like I am doing the same thing that Qazi was doing in the house,” he wrote. “The pain was only to show Qazi that what he did was wrong because he used his health for entertainment, especially when the 15 people in the house were not aware that he was acting and were getting worried for his health.” He added that the promotional material failed to convey the true intention behind the sequence. During the episode, Salman also addressed online trolls who target actors, particularly female artists, over their appearances. He confronted speculation about his health and looks, removing his hat and T-shirt on stage and inviting further trolling. “You guys want to troll me? I will show you. No abs, see my look; you want to troll me now? Go on, troll me,” he said. Salman Khan is scheduled to star in Apoorva Lakhia’s upcoming film Maatrubhumi, for which the release date is yet to be announced.

data.title: Orlando Bloom gets candid about intimate threesome scene with real-life sisters Rooney and Kate Mara
data.incipit: Orlando Bloom is dishing on his “sincere” threesome scene with Rooney Mara and Kate Mara in “Bucking Fastard.” The “Lord of the Rings” actor discussed the intimate moment while presenting the film at the San...
data.body: Orlando Bloom is dishing on his “sincere” threesome scene with Rooney Mara and Kate Mara in “Bucking Fastard.” The “Lord of the Rings” actor discussed the intimate moment while presenting the film at the San Sebastián Film Festival in Spain alongside German writer-director Werner Herzog. “[There is] such simplicity to the characters and [their] carnal desires, but also an innocence to the sisters,” Bloom, 49, said, according to Variety . Orlando Bloom (pictured above at the 2025 Tribeca Festival) opened up about the “sincere” threesome scene he filmed with Rooney Mara and Kate Mara for “Bucking Fastard.” Getty Images for Tribeca Festival “[There is] such simplicity to the characters and [their] carnal desires, but also an innocence to the sisters,” Bloom (seen above with Rooney and Kate in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, in September) said while presenting the film at the San Sebastián Film Festival. Getty Images for IMDb Bloom plays Gareth Mulroney, a “sensitive” man who finds himself caught between twin sisters Joan and Jean Holbrooke, played by real-life sisters Rooney, 41, and Kate, 43, respectively. “Bucking Fastard” is loosely based on the lives of identical twin sisters Freda and Greta Chaplin, per IMDb . Bloom added, “My character, the ‘Bucking Fastard,’ is sensitive too, and he’s quite quickly out of his depth in some ways.” He said the threesome was a “very sincere sort of moment” that he, Rooney and Kate created together. Bloom (pictured above at the San Sebastián Film Festival) plays Gareth Mulroney in “Bucking Fastard,” with Rooney and Kate playing twin sisters Joan and Jean Holbrooke, respectively. Getty Images Bloom said the threesome was a “very sincere sort of moment” that he, Rooney and Kate (all seen above) created together. Getty Images for IMDb Herzog, for his part, also weighed in on the scene, explaining that there are times when a director “has to step back.” He recalled telling Bloom, “You are in bed, and you have two women in your arms. How you deal with it, I cannot give instructions.” Herzog, 84, described the moment as “beautiful,” adding that the scene has “such charm and depth.” German director Werner Herzog (pictured above with Bloom at the San Sebastián Film Festival) explained that there are times when a director “has to step back.” Getty Images Herzog (seen above at the Venice Film Festival with Domhnall Gleeson, Bloom, Rooney and Kate) described the scene as “beautiful,” adding that it has “such charm and depth.” Getty Images The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival on Sept. 3, with Rooney, Kate and Bloom hitting the red carpet together . Rooney and Kate posed side by side, with Rooney sporting Louis Vuitton and Kate donning Armani Privé, while Bloom stepped out in Zegna. Bloom, meanwhile, was most recently photographed vacationing with his daughter , Daisy Dove, and a mystery woman in photos he shared on Instagram on Sept. 12. “Bucking Fastard” premiered at the Venice Film Festival on Sept. 3. (Rooney, Herzog, Kate and Bloom are pictured above on the red carpet.) Dave Bedrosian/Future Image/INSTARimages Bloom (seen above with his ex-fiancée, Katy Perry, their daughter, Daisy Dove, and his son, Flynn, in an Instagram upload) was most recently photographed vacationing with Daisy Dove and a mystery woman. orlando bloom/ instagram He did not give any indication of the woman’s identity. The “Pirates of the Caribbean” actor was most recently romantically linked to Swiss model Luisa Laemmel , 28, after the pair was spotted leaving the Super Bowl together in February. data.title: Strictly fans give their honest verdict on new presenters: 'Three's a crowd'
data.incipit: The Strictly Come Dancing launch show confirmed the celebrity pairings (Picture: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire) Strictly Come Dancing fans have finally had their say over Emma Willis, Johannes Radebe and Josh...
data.body: The Strictly Come Dancing launch show confirmed the celebrity pairings (Picture: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire) Strictly Come Dancing fans have finally had their say over Emma Willis, Johannes Radebe and Josh Widdicombe as the new hosts – and they’re not holding back with their honesty. Tonight, the BBC series finally returned, with lots of changes coming into effect. In addition to Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman being nowhere to be seen, replaced by a trio of presenters, there are also several new pro dancers and, of course, a brand new batch of celebrities, including Dani Dyer , Lacey Turner , Bethany Antonia and Will Best . Before the start of the 2026 series, a lot of longtime viewers had their doubts about the new presenters, as they wondered how the show would work with three personalities fronting the programme. Some naysayers weren’t sure whether Josh would be a good fit given his career as a stand-up comedian, whereas Emma has presented shows like Big Brother and The Voice UK, and Johannes has been a part of Strictly as a professional dancer since 2018. Get personalised updates on Strictly Wake up to find news on your TV shows in your inbox every morning with Metro’s TV Newsletter. Sign up to our newsletter and then select your show in the link we’ll send you so we can get TV news tailored to you. However, plenty of other people defended him, excited to see how he’d bring his dry wit to the ballroom – and now, after the first episode of the season, the verdicts are flying in from fans on social media. A new era of the BBC series begins (Picture: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire) Josh, Emma and Johannes seemed overjoyed to start their new roles (Picture: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire) What do you think of Emma, Johannes and Josh hosting Strictly? I love them! Check I'm not a fan Check I'm undecided Check Writing on X, one Strictly fan called Owen said that Emma was ‘outshining the other two so much’. Several people claimed that ‘three’s a crowd’, while Ryan admitted his believe that Josh was ‘out of place’, adding: ‘I get we can have comic relief but I think Emma & Johannes can do that too 🤷🏼‍♂️.’ ‘3 presenters just seems unnecessary, don’t see the point of it,’ Suzi wrote, while Sue added: ‘The intro was far too long and as for presenters, two’s company three’s a crowd!’ Despite a lot of dubious reactions about the set-up of a trio, and disbelief that the new presenters are the right fit, others were a lot more positive about how Josh, Johannes and Emma handled their first episode. The Strictly pairings have been confirmed, including Dianne Buswell and Will Best (far right) (Picture: Guy Levy/BBC/PA Wire) Josh competed on the Strictly Christmas special with Karen Hauer in 2024 (Picture: BBC Studios/Guy Levy) ‘Josh is doing well. And I was sceptical. This year just feels so fresh and new. Loving it,’ Olivia said. ‘I’m going to be controversial here.... I like Emma, JoJo and Josh!’ wrote Mrs Brightside, while Beverly stated: ‘I wanted to hate the new #Strictly but here I am digging it! Even Josh!’ Another fan called Helen said that she was enjoying the return of Strictly so much that she ‘might be back onboard for this season’, implying that she had been considering giving it a miss. JD added: ‘I really hope people give things chance to bed in and settle. It’s the launch show, nerves are huge and all launches are different to the main show. Just give them all time!’ Who are the Strictly couples for the 2026 series? The full line-up of celebrities and their pro dancer partners are: Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola Graeme Hall and Lauren Oakley Jowita Przystal and Lawrence Robb Will Best and Dianne Buswell Shaun Wright-Phillips and Alexis Warr Melanie Walters and Aljaz Skorjanec Mark Karmalita and Tabby Stoecker, Julian Caillon and Dame Sarah Storey Maddie Ingoldsby and Cach Mercer Chris Appleton and Amy Dowden John Nellis and Katya Jones Carlos Gu and Jaime Winstone Nikita Kuzmin and Dani Dyer Kai Widdrington and Delta Goodrem Nancy Xu and Bethany Antonia Emma, Johannes and Josh were announced as the new presenters of Strictly in May after months of anticipation. Reacting to their newly-appointed roles, Emma said at the time that she’d been a ‘huge fan’ of the show for years. ‘It’s impossible to fill the shoes that Tess and Claudia have left behind – two wonderful, iconic women who have been the beating heart of Strictly for so long. I can only hope that we are able to help to steer the ship as beautifully as they have, into this new chapter.’ she said. Johannes felt ‘deeply honoured’ by his new position, saying that Strictly has ‘always stood for joy, heart and togetherness’. Josh recalled competing in the 2024 Christmas special, expressing that he was ‘giddy with excitement, honoured and a little overawed’. data.title: Hayden Panettiere's Boyfriend Brian Hickerson Reacts to Being Snubbed From Her Memorial
data.incipit: Brian Hickerson reportedly "understands" why he wasn't invited to Hayden Panettiere's upcoming celebration of life.Hickerson, 37, and his brother Zach Hickerson, 38, were both left off the guest list for the...
data.body: Brian Hickerson reportedly "understands" why he wasn't invited to Hayden Panettiere's upcoming celebration of life. Hickerson, 37, and his brother Zach Hickerson , 38, were both left off the guest list for the private memorial honoring the late Nashville star, who died on August 16 at age 36. Despite the snub, sources said the brothers aren't challenging the family's decision. Brian Hickerson 'Understands' the Memorial Snub Brian Hickerson reportedly respects the decision not to invite him to Hayden Panettiere's private memorial.MEGA Sources close to Brian and Zach told TMZ that the brothers recognize the sensitivity surrounding Hayden's memorial and respect the decision not to invite them. Despite being excluded, they reportedly hope the service will be a "beautiful celebration" of Hayden's life and legacy. Brian Hickerson Is Reportedly Struggling With Hayden Panettiere's Death Biran Hickerson is reportedly struggling with the loss of Hayden Panettiere in the weeks following her death.MEGA Brian has reportedly been having an especially difficult time processing the loss. Sources claimed he has lost approximately 40 pounds since Hayden's death and has struggled to regain a sense of normalcy. He reportedly still experiences moments when he expects to hear from her and wishes the tragedy could turn out to be a "horrible dream." Brian and Zach Hickerson Were With Hayden Panettiere When She Died Brian and his brother, Zach Hickerson, were reportedly with Hayden Panettiere when she was found unresponsive in August.MEGA Both brothers were present at the Greenville, S.C., Airbnb where Hayden was found unresponsive. Zach reportedly discovered her, while Brian performed CPR and administered Narcan before emergency responders arrived. Panettiere was ultimately pronounced dead at the scene. Her official cause of death has not been released. Panettiere's representative called reports that she consumed a fentanyl-laced oxycodone pill "unverified hearsay" and stressed that toxicology reports and the investigation remain pending. Hayden Panettiere's Memorial Will Be Held in Malibu Hayden Panettiere will reportedly be honored by family, friends and former colleagues at a private celebration of life in Malibu.MEGA Approximately 150 family members, friends and former colleagues are expected to attend the private service at a church in Malibu, Calif. The coastal location was reportedly selected because of Hayden's love for the ocean and whales. Brian and Zach aren't the only relatives absent from the guest list, as the late star's mother, Lesley Vogel , was also reportedly not invited . Hayden Panettiere and Brian Hickerson Had a Complicated Relationship Hayden Panettiere and Brian Hickerson had an on-again, off-again relationship that dated back to 2018.MEGA Hayden and Brian had an on-again, off-again relationship dating back to 2018. Their history included domestic violence incidents, and Brian pleaded no contest in 2021 to two felony counts of injuring a spouse or girlfriend. The two had reportedly reconnected before Hayden's death, though a source previously claimed she kept the reconciliation private from many friends. Brian and Zach have denied having any involvement in Hayden's death, which remains under investigation.
